configuration.title: LLS CCAI
configuration.autoReloadWindow.descripti: Automatically reload the window after switching the current Claude Code model.
configuration.language.description: Display language for the LLS CCAI settings UI. Auto follows the VS Code display language.
When enabled, one-click Claude Code configuration writes initialPermissionMode=bypassPermissions and allowDangerouslySkipPermissions=true. Recommended only in trusted sandbox environments.
configuration.taskFlow.target.descriptio: Target for sending task-flow prompts. externalClaudeCode keeps the legacy clipboard/focus path; builtinChat sends directly to the built-in Chat when the CLI is available.
configuration.chat.enabled.description: Enable the built-in Chat Webview backed by the local Claude CLI. Disabled by default during Chat migration.
configuration.chat.cliPath.description: Absolute path to the Claude-compatible CLI executable used by the built-in Chat Webview.
configuration.chat.cliArgs.description: Arguments appended when launching the Claude CLI for the built-in Chat.
configuration.chat.cliCwd.description: Working directory for the Claude CLI. Empty means the current active workspace folder.
configuration.chat.transport.description: CLI transport for the built-in Chat Webview. streamJsonStdio is the default long-lived bidirectional stream-json mode; printStdio is a single-request fallback; pty is experimental.
configuration.chat.cliEnv.description: Additional environment variables passed to the Claude CLI. Avoid storing tokens or other sensitive information here.
configuration.chat.permissionMode.descri: --permission-mode value passed to the Claude CLI. acceptEdits is the default and allows Edit/Write/Read-style tools in non-interactive --bare --print mode; default may silently deny tools requiring authorization; bypassPermissions skips all permission checks and should only be used in sandbox environments.
configuration.chat.mcpServers.descriptio: MCP servers passed to the Claude CLI, injected as --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":...}' at startup. Compatible with the official Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code 2.1.x): keys are server names and values describe stdio command/args/env or http/sse url/headers.
configuration.chat.mcpServers.type.descr: MCP server transport type: stdio starts a local subprocess; http/sse calls a remote service; sdk represents an in-process SDK MCP server.
configuration.chat.strictMcpConfig.descr: Append --strict-mcp-config so the Claude CLI ignores other MCP configuration sources such as .mcp.json and only uses servers injected by this extension.
Also read VS Code standard mcp.json configuration (workspace .vscode/mcp.json and user-level mcp.json), so the built-in Chat CLI can see MCP servers configured for VS Code. Top-level servers (VS Code style) and mcpServers (Claude CLI style) are both supported.
configuration.chat.skills.description: Skills allowed when launching the Claude CLI. Matches the SDK options skills field (anthropic.claude-code 2.1.x): 'all' allows every skill; an array of names injects Skill(name) entries into --allowedTools; empty or null means no skill injection.
Enable built-in browser MCP tools for the built-in Chat on VS Code desktop. The tools are enabled by default when desktop support is available; set this to false to disable them. The main Claude CLI can open pages, read content, capture screenshots, inspect console output, and run Playwright/JavaScript in the integrated browser.
configuration.editor.autoOpenReadWriteFi: Automatically open files referenced by Claude Code Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, or NotebookEdit tool calls in the VS Code editor. Files open with preview disabled and without stealing focus.
configuration.vscodeTools.getErrors.enab: Enable the llsccaiVscode MCP server get_errors tool for the built-in Chat. The tool reads current VS Code Problems diagnostics through the extension host.
configuration.chat.currentModel.descript: Current model used by the built-in Chat. Project/workspace value takes precedence over the global value and is passed to the Claude CLI via --model.
configuration.chat.expertMode.project.en: Project-level switch for the on-demand expert (ask_expert MCP tool). When enabled and an expert model is configured, the main Claude CLI can see ask_expert and delegate a self-contained question to an expert sub-request; the full expert trace is visible in the Chat panel but is not written into the main conversation context. This setting overrides the global value; unset falls back to chat.expertMode.global.enabled.
configuration.chat.expertMode.project.mo: Project-level model id used by the expert sub-request. Empty string inherits chat.expertMode.global.model; if the global value is also empty, the expert is unavailable and the main model answers directly. Stored in workspace .vscode/settings.json.
configuration.chat.expertMode.global.ena: Global default switch for the on-demand expert, applied to all workspaces unless a workspace overrides it via chat.expertMode.project.enabled. Stored in user settings and synchronized via Settings Sync.
configuration.chat.expertMode.global.mod: Global default model id for the expert sub-request. Empty string means the expert is unavailable. Project-level chat.expertMode.project.model takes precedence.
configuration.chat.compactionMode.projec: Project-level switch for the dedicated compaction model. When enabled and a model is selected, Claude /compact requests use that model instead of the normal chat model.
Project-level model id used only for Claude /compact requests. Empty string inherits chat.compactionMode.global.model; if none is configured, compaction uses the normal chat model.
configuration.chat.compactionMode.global: Global default switch for the dedicated compaction model, applied to all workspaces unless overridden by the workspace.
Global default model id used only for Claude /compact requests. Project-level chat.compactionMode.project.model takes precedence.
configuration.chat.planMode.project.enab: Project-level switch for the plan task model. When enabled, the dispatcher can delegate design, architecture, and implementation planning work to a separate plan CLI subprocess. This setting overrides the global value; unset falls back to chat.planMode.global.enabled.
configuration.chat.planMode.project.mode: Project-level model id used by the plan subprocess. Empty string inherits chat.planMode.global.model. Stored in workspace .vscode/settings.json.
configuration.chat.planMode.global.enabl: Global default switch for the plan task model, applied to all workspaces unless overridden via chat.planMode.project.enabled. Stored in user settings and synchronized via Settings Sync.
configuration.chat.planMode.global.model: Global default model id for the plan subprocess. Project-level chat.planMode.project.model takes precedence.
configuration.chat.reviewMode.project.en: Project-level switch for the review task model. When enabled, the dispatcher can delegate plan review and quality checks to a separate review CLI subprocess. This setting overrides the global value; unset falls back to chat.reviewMode.global.enabled.
configuration.chat.reviewMode.project.mo: Project-level model id used by the review subprocess. Empty string inherits chat.reviewMode.global.model. Stored in workspace .vscode/settings.json.
configuration.chat.reviewMode.global.ena: Global default switch for the review task model, applied to all workspaces unless overridden via chat.reviewMode.project.enabled. Stored in user settings and synchronized via Settings Sync.
configuration.chat.reviewMode.global.mod: Global default model id for the review subprocess. Project-level chat.reviewMode.project.model takes precedence.
configuration.chat.dispatcher.appendSyst: Optional override for the main CLI (dispatcher) --append-system-prompt text. The main CLI handles everything directly by default and may call the ask_expert tool on demand when needed. Leave empty to use the built-in default prompt.
configuration.chat.expert.appendSystemPr: Optional override for the on-demand expert sub-request --append-system-prompt text. Leave empty to use the built-in default prompt.
configuration.chat.expert.userTriggerMod: How user-triggered expert calls (@llsExpert or /expert prefix) are handled: direct shows the expert answer directly to the user; tool_result writes the expert answer back to the main CLI as a tool_result so the main model continues the turn.
configuration.chat.expert.maxSteps.descr: Maximum number of tool-iteration steps allowed in one ask_expert expert sub-request (default 6).
Per-step timeout for the expert sub-request loop in milliseconds (default 60000).
configuration.chat.expert.totalTimeoutMs: Total timeout for one ask_expert sub-request in milliseconds (default 300000).
configuration.chat.expert.maxCallsPerTur: Maximum number of ask_expert calls allowed within a single dispatcher turn (default 1).
configuration.openapicopilot.systemPromp: System prompt shared with LLS OAI / openapi-compatible-copilot.
